technical_and_design_decisions: Baseline on Java 17 with Spring Framework 6 / Spring Boot 3, consistent with the stated Spring 6.0 requirement.

U1: Implement the RxJava module as a processor using RxJava 3 (io.reactivex.rxjava3), wrapping the message channel adapter so the module can consume an input stream, apply an Observable/Flowable transformation pipeline with backpressure handling, and emit to an output stream.

U2: Deliver as a timeboxed spike only: a design specification document evaluating Spring Security ACL versus a custom metadata-driven ACL model, fit with the XD runtime (admin server, module registry, shell/DSL), and scoped DSL/UI impact; no production ACL code is implemented in this increment.

U3: Deliver as a timeboxed spike: profile admin and container server startup using Java Flight Recorder and async-profiler, analyze hot spots (classpath scanning, bean instantiation, Hadoop client initialization), and document bottlenecks with pros/cons of candidate fixes; no performance refactoring is implemented in this increment.

U4/U5: Use the Apache Hadoop HDFS client configured for NameNode HA (dfs.nameservices with failover proxy) to write the custom module uber-jar to HDFS at deployment time and to read/reinstall it into containers on failure recovery; local disk fallback is retained for development profiles.

U6: Expose the HDFS storage location as an externalized configuration property (e.g., xd.module.hdfs.location) overridable via Cloud Foundry environment variables, resolved through Spring's Environment/property source ordering.

U7: Expose the YARN configuration location as an externalized property (e.g., xd.yarn.config.location) overridable via CF environment variables, feeding the Hadoop Configuration resource loading used by job launchers.

U8: Implement Spark job stop by resolving the running job's YARN application id from the job repository and issuing a kill via the YARN ResourceManager API (Spark fallback), with status reconciliation in the admin server and idempotent error handling for already-terminated jobs.
All new code follows the existing project conventions (Maven build, JUnit 5, Mockito, AssertJ) and integrates with the existing admin/container server modules.
assumptions: U4 and U5 are duplicate user stories describing identical functionality; the work is estimated and performed once.
All work is performed by a single developer; estimates are effort in work-hours, not elapsed duration.
An existing Spring XD-like codebase with admin and container servers, module registry, shell/DSL, and job repository is available and builds cleanly.

Test environments are available at no extra setup cost beyond what is listed: an HDFS cluster with NameNode HA, a YARN cluster running Spark jobs, and a Cloud Foundry environment for override testing.
U2 and U3 are spikes: their outputs are documents (design specs, findings, pros/cons, next steps), not production code.
No new UI is built in this increment; DSL/UI work is limited to the scope analysis documented in the U2 spike.
Estimates include developer-level unit tests within each implementation activity; cross-feature end-to-end integration testing is a separate activity.
Effort excludes product management, release management, and production deployment activities.
Third-party dependencies (RxJava 3, Apache Hadoop client, Spring Framework 6) require no license review or procurement effort.

activities.activity_description: Review the eight user stories, deduplicate U4/U5, confirm spike timeboxes for U2 and U3, define acceptance criteria per story, and sequence the work.
Produce the shared technical design: RxJava processor contract, HDFS HA storage layout for uber-jars, externalized configuration model for CF overrides, and Spark/YARN job-stop flow.
Implement the RxJava-based processor module: module scaffolding, RxJava 3 stream wiring to input/output channels, transformation hook API, backpressure and error handling.
Unit tests for the processor logic (including error and backpressure paths) and module-level integration tests with in-memory channels.

activities.activity_name: U2: ACL spike (research and design specification)
activities.activity_description: Review customer use cases, evaluate Spring Security ACL versus a custom model, assess fit with the XD runtime, scope DSL/UI impact, and document design specs, next steps, and phases.
Set up JFR/async-profiler on admin and container servers, capture startup profiles, isolate CPU bottlenecks, and document root causes with pros/cons of candidate fixes.
Implement writing custom module uber-jars to HDFS on deployment and reading/reinstalling them on container failure recovery, with NameNode HA failover configuration and local-disk fallback.
Unit tests with a mocked/mini HDFS cluster and integration tests covering write, read, reinstall-on-failure, and NameNode failover scenarios.

activities.activity_name: U6: HDFS location override for Cloud Foundry
activities.activity_description: Add externalized property for the HDFS storage location, bind it through Spring Environment so CF environment variables override defaults, and verify resolution with unit and CF-targeted tests.

activities.activity_name: U7: YARN config location override for Cloud Foundry
activities.activity_description: Add externalized property for the YARN configuration location, wire it into Hadoop Configuration resource loading, support CF environment variable override, and add tests.

Implement stop of a running Spark job: resolve the YARN application id from the job repository, invoke the ResourceManager kill API, reconcile job status in the admin server, and handle idempotent/error cases.
Unit tests with mocked ResourceManager/job repository and integration tests against a YARN cluster covering successful stop, already-terminated job, and failure handling.
Cross-feature verification in the HDFS HA, YARN, and Cloud Foundry environments: module deployment with HDFS storage, location overrides, and Spark job lifecycle including stop.
Document the RxJava processor usage, HDFS module storage behavior, the new configuration properties (HDFS and YARN overrides), and the Spark job stop command/API.
Self-review and peer-style review passes over all changes, static analysis cleanup, and rework of identified defects and design issues.
Update Maven modules and dependency management (RxJava 3, Hadoop client), packaging for the new/changed modules, and CI pipeline jobs for the new test suites.
